root_causes.description: The frontend edge service shows a severe p99 tail-latency spike (up to ~7004 ms, approaching the ~7s request timeout ceiling) while its p50/p95 remain ~23-25 ms, so a subset of edge requests stall until they time out/abort, producing the sustained ~1.27 req/s frontend server error rate. All downstream dependencies report zero server errors, localizing the fault to the frontend edge.

The elevated frontend error rate with zero downstream server errors is also consistent with a directly injected HTTP abort at the frontend edge returning failing status codes without a slow dependency. The tail-latency evidence argues against a pure abort, but an injected abort/flag could still contribute.

evidence.observed_value: error_rate mean=1.274 sustained across window; downstream services all 0.000
p99=2178.564 ms with p50=23.427 ms — bimodal latency rather than a uniform abort

root_causes.description: Ruled out as the primary cause: frontend containers show zero restarts over the incident window; the fault manifests as latency and errors rather than pod termination.

remediation_steps: Capture and inspect frontend request traces/logs during the latency window to identify the specific handler or downstream call stalling to the ~7s timeout.
Review the active flagd feature-flag configuration for a frontend latency/timeout injection flag and disable it to validate the fault.
Add circuit-breaking and request timeouts on frontend downstream calls so tail-latency stalls do not convert into edge errors.
Add alerting on frontend p99 tail latency separately from error rate to catch latency-induced aborts earlier.
